problem: LLM-based VLN methods such as NavGPT2 reason only in the language modality and cannot reason about future visual states. Their reasoning module is also frozen or optimized separately from the navigation policy, so the two have conflicting objectives.
motivation: Anticipating what the agent will see after an action should help decisions, especially on long-horizon paths. Existing world-model VLN work (Pathdreamer, DreamWalker, LookAhead) separates state prediction from policy learning, so the prediction is not co-optimized with the policy.
key_idea: A CVAE-based multimodal world model predicts the post-action visual state from partial view, instruction and the chosen node, and a two-stage navigator feeds this prediction back to refine node embeddings and the final action, with the world model and policy trained jointly.
insight: Conditioning the world model on language (cross-attention with instructions) beats a vision-only world model (SR 72.9 vs 71.8 in the R2R val-unseen ablation). Using the predicted state to make the decision matters: the MWM as an auxiliary branch only gives SR 71.5 versus 72.9 with HPFN. Training on the second-stage action a'' alone is best, and combining a' and a'' hurts (SR 72.1, SPL 60.3).
method: Multimodal World Model (MWM): a CVAE whose encoder cross-attends the partial-view embedding of the top-scoring node (query) to instruction features (key/value) over 3 layers, then two MLPs give mu and sigma.

MWM decoder: samples z by reparameterization, concatenates it with the node embedding as condition, and an MLP predicts the future visual-state embedding S_{t+1}. Targets are compressed by a pretrained conv autoencoder to 768-d.
Hierarchical Prediction-Feedback Navigator (HPFN) stage 1: an FFN over topological node embeddings gives a coarse lookahead action a'.
HPFN stage 2: node embeddings (query) cross-attend to the MWM-predicted state (key/value) with residuals, giving V'. An FFN on V' produces the final action a''.

Joint training: it keeps the NavGPT2 BC+DAgger loss. State reasoning is activated only in the first 10% of batches of each phase, and the MWM is periodically retrained as the conditioning features drift.
Plug-in design: applied at fine-tuning on top of NavGPT2 (FlanT5-1.5B, frozen LLM) and DUET, keeping the baselines' pretraining.

setting.backbone: NavGPT2 (FlanT5-1.5B, frozen LLM encoder) with a trained MWM + HPFN; DUET variant for REVERIE
setting.training_data: R2R and REVERIE training data. The baseline pretraining is kept, and UNeMo is added only at fine-tuning. The autoencoder is trained on 30,852 candidate-node views from R2R.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB view features (ViT/LLM encoded) plus language instruction
setting.action_space: discrete node selection on a topological map (nav-graph viewpoints)
setting.privileged: none at test time (training uses ground-truth next-node views as world-model labels)

results: On R2R, UNeMo (FlanT5-1.5B) reaches val-unseen SR 72.1 / SPL 61.1 and test-unseen SR 72.5 / SPL 61.3, beating NavGPT2 FlanT5-5B (SR 72 val-unseen, 71 test-unseen) with less GPU memory (12GB vs 27GB). On REVERIE it improves SR over DUET (val-unseen 49.36 vs 46.98, test-unseen 53.21 vs 52.51) but has slightly lower SPL and RGSPL than the original DUET.
limitations: Only simulator evaluation on R2R and REVERIE, with no real-robot validation (left as future work).
On REVERIE, SPL and RGSPL are lower than the original DUET; the authors attribute this to extra exploratory actions.
Training is a complicated phased schedule (state reasoning active only in 10% of batches, periodic MWM retraining), and the gains are modest, about 2 points of SR.
